newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-WALLACE WIN IN JEOPARDY AS NASCAR IMPOUNDS ENGINE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-WALLACE WIN IN JEOPARDY AS NASCAR IMPOUNDS ENGINE.

text.p: Rusty Wallace is a accomplished master on short tracks, but NASCAR inspectors are checking to see if Wallace had a little help Sunday in winning the 400-mile race at Richmond International Raceway.
The engine from Wallace's Ford Thunderbird was impounded following a post-race inspection for violating NASCAR compression ratio specifications.
The official results of the race are on hold until NASCAR inspectors determine whether Wallace's car violated race rules. No timetable has been established for making the decision.
Should Wallace's engine fail to pass inspection, the race will be awarded to second-place finisher Geoff Bodine, with Dale Jarrett moving up to second and Jeff Gordon to third.
Wallace pulled off what appeared to be his 47th career Winston Cup win and his 21st in 107 short-track starts when he slipped by Jarrett during a restart with four laps to go.

Wallace's record in short-track races is on pace similar to that of Darrell Waltrip (47 wins in 204 starts), while ahead of Dale Earnhardt's impressive career short-track pace (26 wins in 156 starts).

Gordon won the opening two races in the series, and was shooting for an unprecedented three straight wins to open the season. Gordon led the series last season with 10 wins, and Wallace was second with five.
